alternate_boundary_route.note: Same exact boundary theorem; derivative-losing polynomial jet proof. No extra root premise.

optional_existing_stage.role: Optional gluing of equal decoded fields. Not a required edge in the primary chain and not bulk metric gluing.

next_formalization_blocks.purpose: Exact carriers, physical local maps, center evaluation and interval/gauge semantics
Actual Fourier norm derivative, right boundary, native Sobolev-scale composition
Complex Wiener sector, mild uniqueness, mixed analytic bridge
Carrier equivalences, deterministic global maps, both inverses and literal existence corollary

promotion_gates: New exact Lean declarations and their bodies must be prepared without new axioms or admissions.
M1 dependencies require a matching compiler cohort or an explicit source-preserving port into the GR target.
External cached Lean 4.34.0-rc1 compilation and matching theorem-level audit are required for the GR integration.

Audit of an implication never discharges its analytic or semantic hypotheses; the G-goals record those discharges.

goals.name: normalized_forward_restriction_carrier
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Define S_nu(a) as normalized smooth NSE pairs on H=[0,infinity), with equality on H x T3. Equivalently quotient normalized total functions by equality on H. All source predicates descend to this quotient; equality has no negative-time component.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Within smoothness and within derivatives depend only on the forward restriction. The cited congruence results preserve the literal derivative predicates. Spatial derivatives use entire spatial slices at fixed forward t. Initial value and origin gauge are pointwise restrictions. Quotient or restricted-function extensionality therefore gives the exact carrier of Section 1.

goals.name: positive_time_calculus_identification
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For t>0 the literal forward time derivative equals the native GR local time derivative. The spatial gradients, divergences, convections and Laplacians agree after the common Euclidean coordinate definitions are unfolded.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Ici 0 belongs to the neighborhood filter of every t>0. The within-derivative equalities therefore apply. Both spatial definitions use EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 3), the same coordinate vectors, and the same Frechet derivative. No ordinary two-sided time derivative at zero is inferred.

goals.name: forward_pressure_normalization
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: NSSolution(nu,a,u,p) implies NSSolution(nu,a,u,q) and q(t,0)=0 for t>=0, where q(t,x)=p(t,x)-p(t,0). The velocity, initial datum and arbitrary mean are preserved.
goals.mathematical_derivation: The map (t,x)->(t,0) preserves forwardSpacetime and is smooth. Composition and subtraction give joint forward smoothness of q. The subtracted scalar is spatially constant, hence has zero spatial gradient. Periodicity and every remaining NSE predicate are preserved. Analyticity is not needed here.

goals.name: arbitrary_mean_fourier_sobolev_realization
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For every smooth periodic real field b, its actual Fourier coefficients define compatible elements of every TorusSobolev(m); synthesis recovers b pointwise. The squared norm is sum_k <2pi k>^(2m)|bhat(k)|^2, including k=0. Convergence in every H^m is equivalent to spatial C-infinity convergence.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Use generic smooth-datum membership, coefficient reality, rapid decay and the actual coefficient/synthesis inverse. Pointwise Fourier injectivity applies to continuous periodic fields. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives H^m -> C^r for m>r+3/2; the finite derivative L2 expansion gives C^m -> H^m. No mean-zero packaged realization theorem is used.

goals.name: normalized_quadratic_pressure_identity
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Let R(A)hat(0)=0 and R(A)hat(k)=-sum_ij k_i k_j Ahat_ij(k)/|k|^2 for k!=0. Set Q(b,c)=R(b tensor c)-R(b tensor c)(0), Pi(b)=Q(b,b). For m>=2, Q:H^m x H^m -> H^m is continuous bilinear. Every smooth periodic NSE pair satisfies p-p(t,0)=Pi(v) and v_t=F(v):=nu Delta v-P div(v tensor v).
goals.mathematical_derivation: The R symbol has Frobenius operator norm <=1. The Sobolev product estimate and bounded point evaluation prove continuity of Q. Taking divergence of NSE gives Delta p=-div div(v tensor v); the Fourier symbol solves this equation. A periodic harmonic difference has only its zero coefficient, hence is spatially constant. The transport-pressure coefficient i sum_i k_i b_i/(2pi|k|^2), with b_i=2pi i sum_j k_j (v_j v_i)hat, equals the displayed R symbol. The linear torusSobolevPressure is applied to transport coefficients, then normalized; it is not identified directly with Pi.

goals.name: weighted_wiener_banach_algebra
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: A_sigma={c: sum_k exp(sigma|2pi k|)|c(k)|<infinity} is a complex Banach space for sigma>=0. With Euclidean coefficient vectors and Frobenius tensors, ||v tensor w||_(A_sigma)<=||v||_(A_sigma)||w||_(A_sigma). P(0)=I, ||P(k)||<=1, and |(P div A)hat(k)|<=|2pi k||Ahat(k)|.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Multiplication by the positive weight is an isometric isomorphism onto vector-valued ell^1. The exponential triangle inequality bounds the convolution; absolute summability permits reindexing the lattice double sum. The real symmetric orthogonal projection formula, complexified, proves the Euclidean norm-one Leray bound. The default function-space supremum norm is not substituted for the Euclidean norm.

goals.name: smooth_trajectory_wiener_control
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: A supplied jointly smooth periodic trajectory is continuous into A_0 on every compact time interval, with finite uniform A_0 norm there.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Four spatial derivatives give |uhat(k)|<=C<k>^(-4), uniformly on a compact cylinder. The Z^3 majorant is summable. Uniform continuity of the spatial derivatives gives continuity into A_0 by dominated Fourier summation. The native uniform moment theorem is instantiated on the supplied trajectory, not on an unknown global solution.

goals.name: complex_heat_and_duhamel_bounds
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For 0<theta<pi/2, omega>0 and T>0, on S_(theta,T) put sigma(z)=omega sqrt(nu Re z), L=exp(omega^2/4), C=2 exp(omega^2/2)/sqrt(e cos theta). For b in A_0, z->exp(nu z Delta)b is A_0-holomorphic and tends to b in A_0 as z->0 inside the sector. Also ||exp(nu z Delta)b||_(A_sigma(z))<=L||b||_(A_0), and ||B(V,W)||_X<=C sqrt(T/nu)||V||_X||W||_X.
goals.mathematical_derivation: For y>=0, -nu Re(z)y^2+sigma(z)y<=omega^2/4. On compact subsets of the sector, Re z has a positive lower bound, so derivatives of the heat multipliers admit summable coefficient majorants and give A_0 holomorphy. Their moduli are <=1; dominated summation gives strong A_0 convergence to b at zero. For 0<s<1 set b0=nu(1-s)Re z and d=sigma(z)-sigma(sz). Then y exp(-b0 y^2+d y)<=(e b0)^(-1/2)exp(d^2/(2b0)), with d^2/(2b0)<=omega^2/2. Multiplication by |z| and integration of (1-s)^(-1/2), whose integral is 2, give the exact Duhamel constant. The zero-mode divergence is zero.

goals.name: holomorphic_sector_space_complete
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: X consists of A_0-holomorphic maps on S_(theta,T), continuous at 0 into A_0, with finite norm sup_z ||V(z)||_(A_sigma(z)). X is complete; the affine initial-value slice intersected with a closed norm ball is complete.
goals.mathematical_derivation: An X-Cauchy sequence is uniformly A_0-Cauchy. Its limit is continuous at zero and holomorphic by locally uniform convergence. Fatou applied at each z to the weighted coefficient differences preserves each uniform Cauchy estimate, so convergence also holds in X. Initial evaluation and the norm bound define closed sets. Fixed-weight lp completeness alone does not establish this variable-weight space.

goals.name: duhamel_holomorphic_and_closed_ball
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: B(V,W)(z)=-z integral_0^1 exp(nu(1-s)z Delta) P div(V(sz) tensor W(sz)) ds belongs to X and tends to 0 in A_0 as z->0. The map H(V)=exp(nu z Delta)b+B(V,V) preserves the initial-value ball when the constants in G11 are imposed.
goals.mathematical_derivation: For fixed 0<s<1, heat smoothing and bounded convolution give an A_0-holomorphic integrand. On a compact disk inside the sector its norm is bounded by C_D(1-s)^(-1/2). On nested disks, Cauchy gives derivative domination by (C_D/d)(1-s)^(-1/2), an integrable majorant. Thus parameter differentiation under the integral has all required hypotheses. The sqrt(|z|) estimate gives continuity at zero. Holomorphy of the real-valued variable weight is never assumed.

goals.name: periodic_wiener_complex_sector_fixed_point
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For b in A_0 with ||b||_(A_0)<=M and M>0, choose R=2LM and T=nu/(64 C^2 L^2 M^2). There exists a unique fixed point in the complete affine closed ball of radius R; its contraction constant is <=1/2. If k dot bhat(k)=0 for every k, the fixed point is solenoidal. Its zero coefficient is bhat(0), with no mean restriction.
goals.mathematical_derivation: K=C sqrt(T/nu)=1/(8LM), hence KR=1/4. The heat path makes the affine ball nonempty; ||H(V)||<=R/2+R/4 and ||H(V)-H(W)||<=2KR||V-W||. Apply the cited fixed-point theorem on this complete subtype. Fourier divergence of every nonlinear iterate vanishes after projection; the zero coefficient remains bhat(0).

goals.name: physical_nse_projected_mild_equation
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Every supplied smooth NSE trajectory, restarted at s0>=0, satisfies uhat_t(k)+nu|2pi k|^2 uhat(k)=-(P div(u tensor u))hat(k), and therefore the actual A_0-valued heat/Duhamel equation on each compact forward interval.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Differentiate its actual Fourier coefficients under the finite-torus integral, use integration by parts and the pressure projection identity, and integrate the scalar coefficient ODE. G07 and the integrable one-derivative heat bound justify summation and time integration in A_0. This establishes the physical equation required for identification, not just a formal coefficient identity.

goals.name: periodic_wiener_mild_uniqueness
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Two A_0-continuous real-time mild solutions on [0,Tprime], with the same initial value and norms bounded by M0, are equal.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Their difference d satisfies d(t)<=(2M0/sqrt(e nu)) integral_0^t (t-s)^(-1/2)d(s) ds. Choose h>0 with 4M0 sqrt(h)/sqrt(e nu)<1. Taking the supremum on [0,h] forces d=0. Restart the semigroup equation on successive intervals of length <=h; finitely many cover [0,Tprime]. Membership of the supplied smooth solution in the analytic weighted ball is not assumed.

goals.name: identify_analytic_solution_at_every_positive_center
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For every tau>0, the supplied smooth trajectory equals the complex-sector fixed point on a real interval containing tau.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Set M_tau=max(1,sup_[tau/2,tau]||u(s)||_(A_0)), T_tau=nu/(64C^2L^2M_tau^2), h=min(tau/4,T_tau/4), s0=tau-h. Then s0>0 and h lies strictly inside the sector lifetime. G12 and G13 identify the real solutions up to a time strictly beyond h. Thus tau is an interior analytic center. No lower bound for these radii as tau->0 is needed.

goals.name: joint_factorial_bound_and_velocity_analyticity
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: The actual velocity is jointly real analytic on (0,infinity) x T3. On a sufficiently small real cylinder there are C0,A>0 such that ||D^n u||<=C0 A^n n! for every n.
goals.mathematical_derivation: A closed complex time disk admits a fixed positive Fourier weight sigma. Cauchy bounds the mth coefficient derivative by m! R0^(-m) M exp(-sigma|2pi k|). Spatial differentiation and y^r<=r!exp(y) leave a summable exponential margin, giving |d_t^m d_x^alpha u|<=C0 m!|alpha|! R0^(-m)(2/sigma)^|alpha|. Expanding the total n-linear derivative in four coordinate directions gives A=4 max(R0^(-1),2/sigma), since m!|alpha|!<=n!. The actual source is already jointly smooth; the native factorial-bound theorem therefore applies. Separate real analyticity is not substituted for this mixed bound.

goals.name: origin_normalized_pressure_joint_analyticity
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For the actual smooth pressure p of the supplied NSE trajectory, q(t,x)=p(t,x)-p(t,0) is jointly analytic on positive time.
goals.mathematical_derivation: H=-sum_ij partial_i partial_j(u_i u_j) is jointly analytic by G15 and analytic calculus. The native analytic Poisson theorem gives pi=poissonInverse(H) analytic on every positive-time open slab. Since H=Delta p, the actual inverse identity gives pi=p-mean(p); therefore pi-pi(t,0)=p-p(t,0)=q. This discharges the analytic-input hypothesis before using analytic Hodge preservation.

goals.name: positive_time_nse_representative
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: A jointly analytic periodic NSE pair on all positive times defines an actual native NSERepresentative and NSEgerm at every tau>0; one may use radius tau/2.
goals.mathematical_derivation: The slab |t-tau|<tau/2 lies in t>0. Restrict joint analyticity, periodicity and the exact PDE to this slab, using G02 for the derivative conventions when the input is a forward trajectory. Populate the actual AnalyticPeriodicPair and LocalNSE fields and apply NSEgerm.mk. This goal takes positive-time analyticity as its local input; G15 and G16 derive that input from S_nu(a).

goals.name: physical_native_local_equivalence_family
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For every tau>0 choose the actual native c_tau,r_tau,h_tau,i_tau and set E_tau=exactSectorEquivOfContracts c_tau r_tau h_tau i_tau, D_tau=reverseGerm h_tau. Then D_tau E_tau=id and E_tau D_tau=id, with D_tau the actual metric boundary decoder.

Its output supplies all named contracts and the actual inverse laws. The definition of exactSectorEquivOfContracts identifies its maps with the native forwardGerm and reverseGerm. Apply the two existing inverse theorems. Choice of a bare unrelated carrier equivalence would not identify its inverse with the physical decoder.

goals.name: nse_germ_center_velocity
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Define evN_tau:NSEgerm(nu,tau)->Field by evN_tau([u,p])=u(tau). This is independent of the representative and has the displayed computation rule.
goals.mathematical_derivation: SameFlowAt contains eventual equality of the entire velocity field near tau. Evaluation at the center yields equality of fields, so Quotient.lift applies. The quotient computation rule follows from the eliminator. No pressure evaluation on the pressure-gauge quotient is used.

goals.name: gr_germ_center_velocity
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Define evG_tau:GRgerm(nu,rho,tau)->Field by evG_tau([g])=boundaryVelocity(boundaryK(g))(tau). This is independent of the metric representative.

This full-slice equality is required by the spatially nonlocal Leray operator. Evaluate the equality at tau and use Quotient.lift. Neither representative choices nor radii remain in the output.

goals.name: positive_recovery_interval_and_germ_identification
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For tau>0, an actual local NSE representative n at tau and its forward metric representative g admit d>0 with d<=tau/2, d<=n.radius and d<=g.timeRadius, such that v_g=n.velocity and p_g-p_g(t,0)=n.pressure-n.pressure(t,0) throughout |t-tau|<d. Hence evG_tau(E_tau(NSEgerm.mk n))=evN_tau(NSEgerm.mk n), and evN_tau(D_tau gamma)=evG_tau(gamma).
goals.mathematical_derivation: Native forward recovery gives SameFlowAt on a neighborhood R of tau. Apply positive_timeInterval_subset with cap min(tau/2,min(n.radius,g.timeRadius)) and neighborhood R. The cap, rather than the name of that theorem, establishes positive-time containment. Subtract the x=0 gauge equality to obtain exact normalized pressures. ReverseRepresentative has the actual decoded velocity by definition. For analytic local pairs the origin gauge is analytic on the intersection of their slabs, by the cited analytic gauge theorem.

goals.name: positive_time_profile_and_spatial_trace
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Define P_nu^+(a) as pairs (v,q) on (0,infinity) x T3 that are jointly analytic, periodic, solve unforced incompressible NSE, obey q(t,0)=0, and satisfy lim_(t downarrow 0)||v(t)-a||_(H^m)=0 for every m. No temporal derivative or pressure trace belongs to this definition.
goals.mathematical_derivation: The spatial trace is meaningful through the actual coefficient/H^m identification in G04. G05 derives q=Pi(v) from the PDE and gauge; it is not an extra assumption. Equality is equality of these positive-time fields. This is an intermediate carrier; the frozen geometric target remains defined solely by geometric germs, velocity coherence and the spatial trace.

goals.name: coherent_native_nse_family_carrier
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For eta in product_(tau>0) NSEgerm(nu,tau), set W_eta(t)=evN_t(eta_t). Define N_nu^+(a) by: at each tau, some representative n of eta_tau agrees in velocity with W_eta on |t-tau|<d for a 0<d<tau within n.radius; and W_eta(t)->a in every H^m. Coherence is an intrinsic property and is invariant under changing representative after shrinking.
goals.mathematical_derivation: SameFlowAt relates any two representatives by equality of full velocity slices on a neighborhood. Intersect this neighborhood with the old coherence interval, the new representative domain, and t>0; select a symmetric interval with radius at most tau/2. Coherence transfers by equality. The family is a subtype of the dependent product; representative/radius/proof witnesses are not retained as data. Function and subtype extensionality determine equality.

goals.name: coherent_geometric_family_carrier
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: PositiveTimeGRGermFamily is product_(tau>0) GRgerm(nu,rho,tau). Set V_gamma(t)=evG_t(gamma_t). GRForwardFamily(nu,rho,a) is its subtype satisfying DecodedVelocityCoherent and SpatialSmoothInitialTrace(a), exactly as in frozen Section 6. Coherence is intrinsic under representative change.
goals.mathematical_derivation: The metric-germ locality theorem gives equality of decoded full-slice fields on a neighborhood. Intersect with the coherence interval and the new representative domain and shrink below tau/2. This transfers the coherence witness. The trace concerns only V_gamma. No NSE predicate, encoding image, pressure trace, time trace, or common metric collar occurs in the definition. Proof witnesses do not affect subtype equality.

goals.name: coherent_native_family_decodes_to_positive_profile
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For eta in N_nu^+(a), B(eta):=(W_eta,Pi(W_eta)) lies in P_nu^+(a), and [B(eta)]_tau=eta_tau for every tau>0.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Each coherence representative is an analytic LocalNSE pair on a neighborhood. G05 identifies its normalized pressure with Pi(W_eta), since its velocity agrees with W_eta over complete spatial slices. Normalization preserves the analytic local equation. These neighborhoods cover every positive center; thus analyticity, PDE and gauge hold globally on positive time. The inherited trace gives membership of P. Normalized local equality gives SameFlowAt and hence the displayed germ identity.

goals.name: coherent_geometric_family_decodes_to_positive_profile
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For gamma in G_nu,rho^+(a), (V_gamma,Pi(V_gamma)) belongs to P_nu^+(a). On every coherence interval this pair is the origin-normalized actual native boundary decode of the chosen metric representative.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Native reconstruction uses the actual vacuum metric, actual boundary tensor and zero constitutive stress to produce LocalNSE. Restrict to the coherence interval. Full-slice velocity equality and G05 identify the pressure after normalization. Consequently every positive point has an analytic NSE neighborhood. The trace is precisely the admitted spatial trace. No metric gluing or additional geometric premise is used.

goals.name: spatial_jet_polynomial
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Set J_0(b)=b and J_(n+1)(b)=nu Delta J_n(b)-sum_(j=0)^n binom(n,j) P div(J_j(b) tensor J_(n-j)(b)). For m>=2, J_n:H^(m+2n)->H^m is a continuous polynomial of degree <=n+1 and is Lipschitz on each bounded input ball.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Induct in n. The linear Laplacian costs two Sobolev orders. For each product term both lower jets are controlled in H^(m+1) by an input in H^(m+2n+2); use the Sobolev algebra estimate and P div:H^(m+1)->H^m. Finite sums and bounded multilinear compositions preserve polynomial continuity and bounded-ball Lipschitz bounds. The generic Methlib bilinear/Fourier-RHS anchors implement these operations without smallness or a mean-zero premise.

goals.name: time_jet_identities_and_spatial_trace_limits
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For a supplied smooth normalized positive-time NSE pair, partial_t^n v(t)=J_n(v(t)); with K_n(b)=sum_j binom(n,j)Q(J_j(b),J_(n-j)(b)), partial_t^n q(t)=K_n(v(t)). If v(t)->a in every H^m, these converge to J_n(a),K_n(a) in every H^m and after every spatial derivative uniformly.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Differentiate the actual positive-time PDE n times and apply the product rule; this gives precisely the J recurrence. Apply the same rule to q=Q(v,v). Polynomial continuity and the all-order spatial trace give the H^m limits. Sobolev embedding with m>|alpha|+3/2 gives each mixed derivative limit. This is differentiation of an existing trajectory, not an existence theorem for a derivative-losing Frechet ODE.

goals.name: joint_continuous_jet_extension
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: Extend every velocity and pressure mixed jet at zero by the limits in G28. The extended fields are jointly C-infinity on [0,infinity) x T3, with right time jets J_n(a),K_n(a).
goals.mathematical_derivation: For W_n(t)=J_n(v(t)), continuity of W_(n+1) and the positive-time FTC give W_n(t)-W_n(0)=integral_0^t W_(n+1)(s)ds by taking the lower endpoint to zero. Hence the right derivative at zero is W_(n+1)(0). Pack finitely many mixed derivatives of each total order into its symmetric multilinear joint jet. Their component limits give operator-norm continuity. Positive-time derivative identities and continuous linear currying supply the actual hderiv/C tower required by the native closed-halfspace theorem. The same construction applies to pressure. No factorial estimate at zero is claimed.

goals.name: physical_fourier_sobolev_norm_derivative
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For the actual smooth positive-time field v with v_t=F(v), let U_m(t)=Fourier(v(t)) in TorusSobolev(m). Then HasDerivAt U_m (fourierSobolevRhs nu m (U_(m+2)(t))) t for every t>0.
goals.mathematical_derivation: On a compact cylinder around t, every spatial derivative through order m of the difference quotient minus v_t equals integral_0^1 [partial_x^alpha v_t(t+theta h)-partial_x^alpha v_t(t)]dtheta. Uniform continuity makes its C^m norm tend to zero. The C^m-to-H^m estimate and the defining Fourier Hilbert isometry give an actual norm derivative in TorusSobolev(m). Integration by parts, convolution and G05 identify it with the exact fourierSobolevRhs coefficient sequence. Coordinatewise coefficient derivatives alone would not discharge this goal.

goals.name: compatible_fourier_curves_and_right_boundary_equation
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
goals.statement: For any positive-time smooth NSE pair with the spatial trace in G22, put U_m(0)=Fourier(a). Each U_m is ContinuousOn(Ici 0), all U_m share one coefficient sequence at every forward time, and HasDerivWithinAt U_m (F_m(U_(m+2)(t))) (Ici 0) t holds for every t>=0.
goals.mathematical_derivation: Positive-time continuity follows from G30, and the boundary limit is the admitted H^m trace. Compatibility is definitional because every U_m is the same physical coefficient sequence. F_m is continuous, so deriv U_m(t)=F_m(U_(m+2)(t)) tends to F_m(U_(m+2)(0)). Apply hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv with s=Ioi 0. Its differentiability, continuity and derivative-limit premises have now been derived. Combine the boundary result with the positive-time derivative; uniqueDiffOn_Ici identifies the literal within derivative.

goals.name: sobolev_scale_all_forward_time_orders
goals.hypotheses: nu>0; rho!=0 where geometric; a smooth periodic divergence-free with arbitrary mean; only the local inputs stated below
